ip_top_stories.title: Sony Copyright Suit Survives AI Music Generator's Dismissal Bid
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has allowed Sony's copyright infringement lawsuit against an AI music generator to proceed, rejecting the defendant's attempt to have the case dismissed. The ruling is a significant development in ongoing litigation over AI-generated content and music copyright. The case is among several testing the boundaries of copyright law as applied to AI systems.

ip_top_stories.title: Copyright owners v AI developers: the emerging trends
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of the evolving legal landscape between copyright holders and AI developers identifies key emerging trends in how courts and regulators are approaching these disputes. The piece examines patterns across multiple jurisdictions and cases as the volume of AI-related copyright litigation grows. It provides a useful overview of the current state of play for rights holders and technology companies alike.

ip_top_stories.title: Monkey selfie from 15 years ago accidentally sets precedent for AI copyright dispute
ip_top_stories.summary: The landmark 'monkey selfie' case, which established that non-human authors cannot hold copyright, is now being cited as an inadvertent precedent in disputes over AI-generated content. Legal observers note the ruling's logic — that copyright requires human authorship — is directly relevant to questions about who, if anyone, owns AI-produced works. The article examines how a decade-old wildlife photography case is shaping emerging AI copyright doctrine.

ip_top_stories.title: EU copyright law roundup – first trimester of 2026
ip_top_stories.summary: IPKat's quarterly roundup covers the key EU copyright law developments from the first three months of 2026, including legislative updates, court rulings, and regulatory activity relevant to AI and intellectual property. The summary provides a comprehensive overview of how EU frameworks are evolving in response to AI-related copyright challenges. It is a key reference for practitioners and publishers operating across European jurisdictions.

ip_top_stories.title: Is the government's stance on AI copyright holding back the UK tech scene?
ip_top_stories.summary: The article examines whether the UK government's current approach to AI copyright — including proposed text and data mining exceptions — is hampering the country's technology sector competitiveness. It sets out arguments from both the AI industry and rights holders about the implications of the policy. The debate reflects broader tensions between supporting AI development and protecting creators' rights.

ip_further_links.title: AI Makes Securing Copyright Protection for Software Code Tricky Guide
ip_further_links.summary: A guide examining the growing complexity of obtaining copyright protection for software code produced with AI assistance, outlining the key legal uncertainties developers and companies face.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of how a recent Anthropic coding incident has highlighted unresolved contradictions in how copyright law applies to AI-generated software code.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated content should be clearly labelled to help people spot fakes, committee says — The Globe and Mail
ip_further_links.summary: A parliamentary or regulatory committee has recommended that AI-generated content carry clear labels to assist the public in identifying artificially produced material.

ip_further_links.title: Analysing China's stricter examination standards for AI-related patent applications
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of China's tightened patent examination standards for AI-related inventions, with implications for how AI innovations are protected under Chinese intellectual property law.

ip_further_links.title: Bologna Children's Book Fair 2026: AI Takes Center Stage [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: AI was a dominant theme at this year's Bologna Children's Book Fair, with publishers and creators debating its implications for children's publishing, illustration, and intellectual property.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Don't believe the hype. Believe the data.
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines what the data actually shows about AI's impact on the patent industry, challenging some widely circulated claims about AI's transformative role in patent filing and prosecution.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Exploring Data Spaces in Scholarly Communications
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines the emerging concept of data spaces in scholarly publishing, with implications for how research data is shared, governed, and potentially used for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns AI copyright when machines create art?
ip_further_links.summary: A broad explainer examining the unresolved legal question of copyright ownership in AI-generated artworks, surveying current positions across different jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: GitHub Policy Update
ip_further_links.summary: GitHub has updated its policies in ways relevant to AI-generated code, copyright, and intellectual property rights for software developers using the platform.

ip_further_links.title: AI Startups Have These Copyright Lawyers on Speed Dial
ip_further_links.summary: A report on the growing demand for specialist copyright legal counsel among AI startups navigating the complex intellectual property risks of training and deploying AI models.
